overview.title: Overview
overview.body:
# Overview
Catan is a trading and building game.

Players collect resources, trade with each other, and build roads, settlements, and cities.

The game is about expanding to good locations, managing scarce resources, and negotiating with the other players.

goal.title: Goal of the Game
goal.body:
# Goal
The goal is to be the first player to reach **10 victory points**.

You get victory points mainly from:

- settlements
- cities
- some development cards
- Longest Road
- Largest Army

board.title: The Board
board.body:
# The Board
The board is made of hexes.

Each land hex produces one type of resource. Most land hexes also have a number token.

When that number is rolled, the hex produces resources for players with buildings next to it.

The desert does not produce resources.

resources.title: Resources
resources.body:
# Resources
There are five resources:

- **Brick**
- **Lumber**
- **Wool**
- **Grain**
- **Ore**

You use resources to build things.

Typical uses:

- Roads need brick and lumber.
- Settlements need brick, lumber, wool, and grain.
- Cities need grain and ore.
- Development cards need wool, grain, and ore.

settlements-and-roads.title: Settlements, Cities, and Roads
settlements-and-roads.body:
# Settlements, Cities, and Roads
A **settlement** is built on an intersection between hexes.

A settlement is worth **1 victory point** and produces **1 resource** when an adjacent hex produces.

A **city** upgrades one of your settlements. It is worth **2 victory points** and produces **2 resources** from adjacent hexes.

A **road** is built along an edge between hexes. Roads let you expand to new building spots.

setup.title: Setup
setup.body:
# Setup
Each player begins with:

- 2 settlements
- 2 roads
- some starting resources from their second settlement

When placing starting settlements, look for:

- good numbers
- useful resource variety
- access to brick and lumber for early roads
- access to ore and grain for cities and development cards
- ports, if they support your resource plan

Important rule: settlements must be at least **two edges apart** from any other settlement or city.

turn-structure.title: Turn Structure
turn-structure.body:
# Turn Structure
On your turn:

1. Roll the dice.
2. Everyone collects production from the rolled number.
3. You may trade.
4. You may build.
5. You may play up to one development card, if allowed.

Trading and building can usually be done in any order after production.

production.title: Production
production.body:
# Production
Roll two dice.

Each hex with the rolled number produces resources.

If you have a settlement next to that hex, take **1 matching resource**.

If you have a city next to that hex, take **2 matching resources**.

All players collect at the same time, not only the active player.

If a 7 is rolled, no hex produces.

trading.title: Trading
trading.body:
# Trading
After rolling, the active player may trade.

There are two main kinds of trade:

## Player trading
The active player may trade resources with other players. Other players may only trade with the active player.

## Bank and port trading
You may trade with the bank at a fixed rate.

Ports can give better trade rates if you have a settlement or city on that port.

Trading is often the heart of the game. You usually cannot build everything alone.

building.title: Building
building.body:
# Building
You spend resources to build.

Common builds:

- **Road**: helps you expand.
- **Settlement**: gives a new point and new production.
- **City**: improves a settlement and doubles production.
- **Development card**: gives a hidden card with a useful effect.

A new settlement must connect to your road network and must obey the distance rule: no adjacent settlement or city.

development-cards.title: Development Cards
development-cards.body:
# Development Cards
Development cards are bought with resources and kept hidden.

They may give:

- knights
- progress effects
- hidden victory points

Usually, you cannot play a development card on the same turn you bought it.

You may play at most one development card on your turn.

Victory point cards are different: they stay hidden until you reveal them to win.

robber.title: The Robber
robber.body:
# The Robber
The robber matters when a **7** is rolled or when a knight is played.

When a 7 is rolled:

1. Players with too many resource cards must discard half.
2. The active player moves the robber to a hex.
3. That player steals one random resource from a player with a settlement or city next to that hex.

A hex with the robber does not produce resources.

longest-road-largest-army.title: Longest Road and Largest Army
longest-road-largest-army.body:
# Longest Road and Largest Army
There are two special awards worth **2 victory points** each.

## Longest Road
Awarded to the player with the longest continuous road, once it is long enough.

It can be taken away if another player builds a longer road.

## Largest Army
Awarded to the player who has played the most knights, once enough knights have been played.

It can also be taken away if another player plays more knights.

ending.title: Game End
ending.body:
# Game End
The game ends when a player reaches **10 victory points** on their own turn.

Remember that some victory points may be hidden in development cards.

A player may reveal hidden victory point cards when they have enough points to win.

first-turn-summary.title: First Turn Summary
first-turn-summary.body:
# First Turn Summary
On your turn, remember:

1. Roll the dice.
2. Everyone collects resources from the rolled number.
3. If you rolled 7, resolve the robber instead.
4. Trade if you want.
5. Build if you can.
6. Optionally play one development card, if allowed.

Beginner advice:

- Try to get more settlements early.
- Trade actively.
- Watch who is close to 10 points.
- Do not ignore ore and grain; cities are powerful.
